result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS for the REVIEWER idiom and scope gate on REQ-466 at afb62fde. No code defect and no stray edit. findings.description: The narrowing is cited as following the 'Q-1044 pattern' (this line; also handoffs/WF02-REQ466-20261013/step-02-elixir-dev.json lines 70 and 134). Q-1044 does not support narrowing. Its acceptance criterion 1 requires exactly the six approval ids on the escalation node (Q-1044 report lines 22 and 25), and it avoided the same-role pair by rerouting the escalation to a non-approver role (lines 6-7). What Q-1044 does support is leaving the guard unchanged (lines 11-12; recorded at docs/requirements.yaml:35190). REQ-459 design section 9 decision 2 (lib/letflow/design/req459-required-outputs-and-distinct-person.md:765-766) says a later node must name the escalation node's id too. The fixture's appended sentence states the narrowing and its cause but does not call it a departure from those records. The pre-existing sentence 'Deviations (documented, no waivers): none' at test/fixtures/qa/vortex_production_order_release_process_definition.json line 4 stays in place under the no-rewrite rule, so the record has to live elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Record the narrowing as a departure from REQ-459 section 9 decision 2 and Q-1044 acceptance criterion 1 (via F-01), and stop describing it as following the Q-1044 pattern. Do not edit the v1.7 description in place; a wording change to a published version needs its own version decision. No code change.
